properties.name: timeText
properties.notes: The curved status strip's text. Frozen rather than live: a design whose render changed every minute could not be diffed. Empty draws no strip, which is `ScreenScaffold` without a `timeText` argument.

properties.name: scrollIndicator
properties.notes: Whether the generated screen gives `ScreenScaffold` a scroll indicator. The canvas draws none either way: an indicator shows where a viewport sits in the content, and the long-screenshot extent has no viewport. The real capture agrees — a `ScrollMode.LONG` render sets `LocalScrollCaptureInProgress` and the emitted scaffold suppresses the indicator while it is set, which is what keeps a stitched capture free of the dashes an indicator drawn per frame leaves down the edge.

svg.notes: The stadium screen frame has not been through structured SVG parity.

wasm.notes: Drawn as a Wear long-screenshot stadium at the document frame's width, with the content padding the real `ScreenScaffold` computes for that screen size, the clock where `AppScaffold` puts it, and a bezel scroll indicator. It is not Wear Compose — `androidx.wear.compose:compose-material3` is an Android AAR the Wasm canvas cannot link — but it is measured against it: wear-m3-catalog's stitched `ScrollMode.LONG` capture of the same list matches this to within a dp.

properties.name: transformation

svg.notes: An untransformed stand-in must not claim structured SVG parity with the real list.

wasm.notes: Drawn as a plain Column at the list's own spacing. That is what a stitched `ScrollMode.LONG` capture of the real one is: `LONG` turns the row transformation off in order to stitch, so every row on the reference is full content width at every position and the Column reproduces it exactly. What neither shows is a live frame, where `SurfaceTransformation` scales and fades a row by its distance from the bezel; the generated Kotlin emits that, and a single-frame render is what draws it.

wasm.notes: Uses the common CMP player. Each named UI Builder slot registers the matching Remote Compose custom-component config.

svg.notes: The subtree becomes a Remote Compose document at export; SVG export of one needs an explicit renderer, exactly as remote-compose/document does.

wasm.notes: The subtree is drawn with the ordinary Compose stand-ins remote-m3 already uses, inside a marked frame. The canvas has no Remote Compose writer, so until the subtree is captured these are the shapes the generated @RemoteComposable body describes rather than the pixels a player produces. A host that captures it - compiling the generated body and running captureSingleRemoteDocument on the Android daemon - answers with a document, and the same frame then plays it through the player that draws an embedded remote-compose/document, with the design's own custom components registered by name.

properties.name: name
properties.notes: The custom-component config name the document writes and the host registers a renderer under. Namespaced by convention (slot:, rc:, or an application domain) so two documents composed together cannot collide.

properties.name: widthDp
properties.notes: The bounds the document reserves for host content it cannot measure. A player lays out a custom component from the document, not from the Compose content filling it.

properties.name: heightDp
properties.notes: See widthDp.

svg.notes: Host content inside a Remote Compose document has no structured SVG answer.

wasm.notes: Draws the ordinary Compose content in its own slot, which is what a registered renderer draws on a real player too. A preview only draws it if a custom component of this name is registered; an unregistered one is a player support issue rather than silently borrowed content. The code mapping names the registry rather than a composable, because the composable is whatever the host registers under this name.

adapterStatus.planned: The Compose API is available to Wasm but the catalog authoring adapter is not implemented yet.
adapterStatus.supported: Implemented by the current candidate document renderer.
adapterStatus.unsupported: No verified Wasm execution path exists; documents may retain the node but clean render and export must fail visibly.

assetRegistry.$comment: Every assetKey the catalog itself ships, because these are the assets the canvas draws from its own resources: the two project-owned Jetcaster covers in :ui-builder-artwork, the generated gate-0 cover, and the editor's own insert placeholder. A design extends this set with the keys its assets map pins through the asset lane (PUT /api/ui-builder/v1/designs/{designId}/assets/{assetKey}, ui_builder_put_asset; yschimke/compose-preview-server#478). Both reducers refuse any other key at commit (#484).

colorTokens.$comment: The theme roles a colour property or a background modifier may name, which are the roles the canvas draws. A colour is otherwise a #RRGGBB or #AARRGGBB literal. Mirrored by PropertyValueKinds.CANVAS_COLOR_TOKENS in :ui-builder-export and by the runtime's catalog executor; a test pins the three to this list.

wasm.reason: The canvas is Compose Multiplatform for Wasm and Wear Material 3 is an Android AAR, so every Wear component here is drawn by its nearest Material 3 lookalike. Author on it; do not read a size, a colour or a shape off it. The Android preview compiles this design's own generated Kotlin against real Wear Compose.

svgStatus.raster-fallback-required: The component may export only as a named embedded raster fallback.
svgStatus.unsupported: No honest SVG or declared fallback exists; export must fail.
svgStatus.unverified: The composite SVG spike has not proved this dynamic component; export remains gated.
svgStatus.verified: Proved for this frozen benchmark's authored usage through the pinned same-runtime JVM Skia recorder; this does not verify unused variants or other environments.
